definitions.explanation: A stereotypical stubborn, old-fashioned father or older man who refuses to bend — strict, set in his ways, and gruff. Often used half-affectionately.

examples.japanese: うちの{父|ちち}は{頑固親父|がんこおやじ}だ。
examples.english: My dad is a stubborn old man.

examples.japanese: {頑固親父|がんこおやじ}が{営|いとな}むラーメン{屋|や}。
examples.english: a ramen shop run by an obstinate old master

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}の{頑固親父|がんこおやじ}は{子供|こども}に{厳|きび}しかった。
examples.english: Stubborn fathers of the old days were strict with their children.

notes:
A common stereotype, often applied half-affectionately to a gruff, principled older man — including the {頑固親父|がんこおやじ} of a long-established restaurant who won't compromise on quality.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {頑固|がんこ}: stubborn — the underlying adjective (-na)
- {親父|おやじ}: dad; old man — a casual word for one's father or a middle-aged-to-older man

USAGE:
Somewhat colloquial; the tone ranges from exasperated to admiring.
